# Physics Lab

> A free virtual physics lab for students and teachers: 15 interactive simulations of motion, forces, energy, waves, circuits and light, each with a lesson, a printable classroom activity and a teacher answer key, plus a formula sheet and a list of physics symbols. Runs in the browser with no sign-up. From the makers of Interactive Periodic Table.

## Tools

- [Physics Simulations: 15 Free Interactive Online Experiments](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/): Physics simulations to run free in your browser: 15 interactive experiments on motion, forces, energy, waves, circuits and optics, with worked formulas.
- [Buoyancy Simulation & Buoyant Force Calculator (F = ρgV)](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/buoyancy/): Buoyancy simulation: set object density, fluid density, volume and immersion to find the buoyant force F = ρgV and see whether the object floats or sinks.
- [Circular Motion Simulation & Centripetal Force (F = mv²/r)](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/circular-motion/): Circular motion simulation: set mass, radius and speed to find centripetal force F = mv²/r, acceleration and period for a string, a car or a satellite.
- [Collision Simulation: Elastic and Inelastic Momentum Lab](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/collisions/): Collision simulation for two carts: set masses, velocities and restitution to compare elastic and inelastic collisions, momentum and kinetic energy lost.
- [Conservation of Energy Simulation: PE & KE on a Ramp](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/energy-conservation/): Conservation of energy simulation: slide a block down a frictionless ramp and track height, speed, PE = mgh and KE = ½mv² while the total stays constant.
- [Force and Friction Simulation & Calculator (f = μN)](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/force-and-friction/): Force and friction simulation: set mass, push and friction coefficient to find the friction force (f = μN = μmg), net force and acceleration of a block.
- [Free Fall Simulation: Acceleration Lab with Air Resistance](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/free-fall/): Free fall virtual lab: drop an object under Earth, Moon, Mars or Jupiter gravity, with or without air resistance. Read fall time, speed and acceleration.
- [Motion Graphs Simulator: Position, Velocity & Acceleration](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/motion-graphs/): Motion graphs simulator for constant acceleration: set initial velocity and acceleration, then read position and velocity at any time from two live graphs.
- [Ohm’s Law Simulation & Power Calculator: V = IR, P = VI](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/ohms-law/): Ohm’s law simulation and power calculator: set the voltage and resistance of a simple circuit to find the current I = V/R and power P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
- [Pendulum Simulation & Period Calculator: T = 2π√(L/g)](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/pendulum/): Pendulum simulation and period calculator: change length, gravity and starting angle to find the period T = 2π√(L/g) and frequency, then watch it swing.
- [Projectile Motion Simulator & Calculator](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/projectile-motion/): Free projectile motion simulator: set launch speed, angle and gravity, watch the path, and read the range, peak height and flight time with worked steps.
- [Refraction & Total Internal Reflection Simulation](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/refraction/): Snell’s law refraction simulation: set two refractive indices and the incident angle to see refraction, the critical angle and total internal reflection.
- [Resistors in Series and Parallel Simulation & Calculator](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/resistor-circuits/): Resistors in series and parallel simulation: set a supply voltage and two resistances to compare equivalent resistance, total current and branch currents.
- [Spring Oscillator Simulation: Hooke’s Law, Period & Energy](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/spring-oscillator/): Mass on a spring simulation: set mass, spring constant and amplitude to find the period T = 2π√(m/k), displacement, velocity and energy of the oscillation.
- [Converging Lens Simulation & Thin Lens Calculator](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/thin-lens/): Converging lens simulation: set the focal length and object distance to see the ray diagram, a real or virtual image, image distance and magnification.
- [Wave Simulator: Wavelength, Frequency & Wave Speed](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/wave-explorer/): Interactive transverse wave simulation: change amplitude, wavelength and frequency to see wave speed v = fλ and period, and track how one particle moves.

## Lessons

- [Physics Lessons with Formulas & Worked Examples](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/): Fifteen short physics lessons on motion, forces, energy, waves, circuits and optics, each with key formulas, a worked example and an interactive simulation.
- [Buoyancy Formula & Archimedes’ Principle Explained](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/buoyancy/): Archimedes’ principle and the buoyancy formula F = ρgV explained: why objects float or sink, how to find the submerged fraction, and a step-by-step example.
- [Centripetal Force Formula F = mv²/r & Circular Motion](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/circular-motion/): Uniform circular motion explained: centripetal acceleration a = v²/r, centripetal force F = mv²/r, period, why centrifugal force misleads, and a worked example.
- [Momentum & Collisions: Elastic vs Inelastic, with Formulas](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/collisions/): Conservation of momentum for elastic and inelastic collisions: p = mv, the coefficient of restitution, impulse, kinetic energy lost and a worked example.
- [Conservation of Mechanical Energy: Formula & Worked Example](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/energy-conservation/): Conservation of mechanical energy: without friction, PE + KE stays constant, so mgh = ½mv² and v = √(2gh). Formulas, a worked ramp example and a simulation.
- [Friction Formula f = μN: Static vs Kinetic Friction](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/force-and-friction/): Learn the friction formula f = μN (f = μmg on level ground), the difference between static and kinetic friction, and how to find the net force and acceleration.
- [Free Fall Formulas: v = gt, h = ½gt² & Terminal Velocity](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/free-fall/): Free fall explained: why every mass falls at g without air, the formulas v = gt, h = ½gt² and t = √(2h/g), how terminal velocity arises, and a worked example.
- [Position, Velocity & Acceleration: Equations and Graphs](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/motion-graphs/): How position, velocity and acceleration are related: read slopes and areas on motion graphs, use v = v₀ + at and x = v₀t + ½at², and follow a worked example.
- [Ohm’s Law & Power Formulas: V = IR and P = VI = I²R](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/ohms-law/): Ohm’s law and the electrical power formula explained: V = IR, I = V/R and P = VI = I²R = V²/R, with units and a step-by-step worked example.
- [Simple Pendulum Period Formula: T = 2π√(L/g) Explained](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/pendulum/): The simple pendulum formula T = 2π√(L/g) explained: why mass does not matter, how length and gravity change the period, and a step-by-step worked example.
- [Projectile Motion Formulas: Range, Max Height & Flight Time](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/projectile-motion/): Projectile motion formulas explained: range R = v₀² sin 2θ/g, maximum height, time of flight and horizontal launches, with a step-by-step worked example.
- [Snell’s Law, Refraction & Total Internal Reflection](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/refraction/): Snell’s law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ explained: why light bends toward the normal, how to find the critical angle, and when total internal reflection happens.
- [Resistors in Series & Parallel: Formulas and Examples](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/resistor-circuits/): Formulas for resistors in series (R = R₁ + R₂) and parallel (1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂), voltage and current dividers, and a worked example for each circuit.
- [Spring Oscillator: Hooke’s Law, Period & Energy in SHM](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/spring-oscillator/): Simple harmonic motion of a mass on a spring: Hooke’s law F = −kx, the period T = 2π√(m/k), maximum speed and energy, with a step-by-step worked example.
- [Thin Lens Equation: Converging Lens Images & Ray Diagrams](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/thin-lens/): Use the thin lens equation 1/f = 1/dₒ + 1/dᵢ and magnification M = −dᵢ/dₒ to predict real and virtual images from a converging lens, with a worked example.
- [What Is a Wave? Wavelength, Frequency & v = fλ](https://thephysicslab.org/learn/wave-explorer/): What is a wave in physics? Learn amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period and the wave equation v = fλ, with a transverse-wave diagram and a worked example.

## Reference

- [Physics Formulas Sheet: Motion, Forces, Energy & Circuits](https://thephysicslab.org/formulas/): Physics formulas sheet by topic: projectile motion, friction (f = μmg), energy, buoyancy, waves, Ohm’s law, series and parallel resistors, and lenses.
- [Physics Symbols: List of Symbols, Meanings and Units](https://thephysicslab.org/physics-symbols/): List of physics symbols with their meanings and SI units: F for force, d for distance, v for velocity, μ for friction, λ for wavelength and Ω for the ohm.
- [Physics Units & Constants Reference](https://thephysicslab.org/units/): SI units for physics: metres, seconds, kilograms, newtons, joules, watts, hertz, volts, amperes and ohms, plus g = 9.81 m/s², degrees vs radians, and prefixes.

## Classroom

- [Physics Practice Problems with Answers & Explanations](https://thephysicslab.org/practice/): Free physics practice problems with answers: 100 multiple-choice questions on motion, forces, energy, waves, electricity and optics, each fully explained.
- [The Physics Lab for Teachers: Free Simulations & Classroom Activities](https://thephysicslab.org/teachers/): Free physics simulations with printable student worksheets, answer keys and NGSS connections. Share any experiment to Google Classroom; no logins, works on Chromebooks.
- [Free Printable Physics Worksheets with Answer Keys](https://thephysicslab.org/worksheets/): Free printable physics worksheets with answer keys: build an 8-, 12- or 20-question sheet by topic, or print a one-page activity on buoyancy or circuits.
- [Buoyancy & Floating Worksheet: Free Student Activity](https://thephysicslab.org/experiments/buoyancy/activity/): Free printable buoyancy & floating worksheet for grades 7–12, about 25 minutes with the interactive simulation. No sign-up; answer key for teachers.

## About

- [About The Physics Lab — Free Visual Physics Learning](https://thephysicslab.org/about/): The Physics Lab is a free, independent collection of interactive physics simulations, lessons, and practice. Learn how its models, numbers, and data work.
- [Privacy Policy](https://thephysicslab.org/privacy/): How The Physics Lab handles your privacy: no accounts, Google Analytics usage statistics, no ads, and practice scores kept in your browser.
